Chapter Four: Authenticity and the End of People-Pleasing
Now that we've laid the groundwork with self-respect and independence, let's talk about the next big step—embracing authenticity.
Being authentic means showing up as your true self, without putting on a mask or bending over backwards just to make others happy. It’s about letting your real thoughts, feelings, and preferences come through, even if they aren’t exactly what your partner expects.
Think about people-pleasing for a moment. It's something so many of us fall into, especially if we’re worried about conflict or being rejected. Maybe you’ve said “yes” to things that didn’t feel right, kept your opinions to yourself, or just went along with someone’s plans to keep the peace.
But here’s the thing—while people-pleasing might seem to smooth things over in the short run, it actually chips away at who you are. After a while, the person who always says “yes” starts to disappear. Her real needs and desires get buried under layers of trying to please everyone else.
Authenticity, on the other hand, is refreshing. It brings real connection. When you’re open about what you like, what you don’t, and where your boundaries are, you give your partner a chance to see—and appreciate—the real you. You’re not afraid to disagree, to ask for what you want, or even to walk away from things that just don’t fit your values.
So, how can you start bringing more authenticity into your relationships? Here are a few simple practices:
Express your opinions and preferences honestly, even if they’re different from your partner’s. Speak up about how you’re feeling, without worrying about being judged or rejected. When you feel the urge to just go along to keep things smooth, pause—and check in with what you really want. Remember, being true to yourself is always more attractive than saying “yes” to everything.
Picture this: a woman gets invited to an event that just doesn’t interest her. Instead of forcing herself to go just to avoid disappointment, she politely says no and, if she wants, shares her reasons. Sure, her partner might be a little let down, but he also learns to respect her honesty and her individuality. Over time, that kind of honesty builds real trust and admiration.
Being authentic also means being clear about what you want and expect in your relationship. Don’t wait for your partner to guess what you need—let them know directly. This kind of clarity keeps misunderstandings at bay and makes sure both of you are on the same page.
Making the shift from people-pleasing to authenticity is freeing. It brings deeper connection, stronger self-respect, and a more balanced dynamic. When you’re not afraid to be yourself, you’re not just happier—you become someone others are drawn to, someone whose strength and honesty truly shine.
